Where the Meshes Disagree

The coarse and medium meshes differ by 21–24 drag counts. These figures locate it. All three wings are drawn at one common scale with axes in metres, and the sectional plots use the standard convention — suction upward, both surfaces, levels overlaid.

The last 5 % of chord gives −9.2 to −10.3 counts in all six cases — three wings, two incidences, a spread of barely one count. That band is 40–45 % of the whole difference, from 5 % of the chord. The mid-chord, 40 % of the surface, contributes ±2 counts.

—reading

What these change

  • It is an edge problem, not a chordwise-resolution problem. Sharper than what I had been saying. Refining the whole chord works because it also refines the edges — 40 % of the surface contributes ±2 counts.
  • The trailing edge is the single most reproducible term, −9.2 to −10.3 counts across three wings and two incidences. The blunt base is 0.1 % of chord with three nodes across it.
  • This independently supports family 2's edges=True. I added it on a 7 % argument; this says the edges carry closer to 80 %.
  • Not a tip or wake effect — the spanwise split follows area. Another independent line against the wake hypothesis retracted earlier.

The test this argues for: hold every count fixed and refine only ds_te_frac. If the trailing-edge band is the mechanism, that recovers most of 10 counts for almost no cells.

Surface solutions from runs/s8_v2/g{83,47,13}/{gci_C,gci_M}_a{0,4,8}. The drag decomposition reproduces each run's recorded C_Dp to 0.000 counts at α 0 and 0.05 at α 4, the residual being the tip-cap zone, excluded here.
